Let `(G, ι)` be a binary phylogenetic `X`-tree with path-length metric `d` for positive edge lengths `w`, whose internal edges have length at least `m > 0`, and let the sites be pairwise independent and identically distributed, with the two-leaf marginals of the JC model with rate…

Let `(G, ι)` be a binary phylogenetic `X`-tree with path-length metric `d` for edge lengths `w`, and let the sites be pairwise independent and identically distributed, with the two-leaf marginals of the JC model with rate `μ` and uniform root: for every path `p` from `x` to `y`,…

nodes.summary: Parsimony is inconsistent in the Felsenstein zone (Felsenstein 1978): if the sites `σ i` are pairwise independent and identically distributed with the pattern distribution of the quartet, and `0 ≤ Q < 1/2`, `P ^ 2 > Q (1 - Q)`, then almost surely, for all long enough alignments, the wrong quartet `AC | BD` has a strictly smaller total Fitch score than the true quartet `AB | CD` and the third quartet `AD | BC`.
nodes.title: Parsimony is inconsistent in the Felsenstein zone

nodes.summary: For pairwise independent, identically distributed sites, the empirical p-distance of every pair of taxa converges almost surely to the probability that the two taxa differ at a site.
nodes.title: Strong law for the p-distances

nodes.summary: The Felsenstein zone (Felsenstein 1978): if `0 ≤ Q < 1/2` and `P ^ 2 > Q (1 - Q)`, the wrong quartet `AC | BD` has strictly smaller expected parsimony score per site than both the true quartet `AB | CD` and the third quartet `AD | BC`. The statement is algebraic in `P`; the model has `0 ≤ P ≤ 1/2`.
nodes.title: The Felsenstein zone

nodes.summary: The expected Fitch parsimony score of one site on the quartet `((a, b), (c, d))`.
nodes.title: Expected Fitch parsimony score on a quartet

nodes.summary: A reversible continuous-time model gives a reversible semigroup: if `π` is in detailed balance with the generator `Q`, the transition functions `exp (t • Q)` form a reversible semigroup for `π`.
nodes.title: Reversible continuous-time models give reversible semigroups

nodes.summary: A family of transition matrices `P t`, indexed by branch length, is a reversible semigroup for the distribution `π`: it satisfies the Chapman–Kolmogorov equation and detailed balance `π a P t a b = π b P t b a`. With rows summing to `1`, detailed balance makes `π` stationary; the pulley principle uses only the two equations below.
nodes.title: Reversible semigroup of transition matrices

nodes.summary: JC-corrected distances are path lengths (Jukes & Cantor 1969): the JC distance of the probability that the two ends of a path differ is `μ` times the total branch length.
nodes.title: JC-corrected distances are path lengths

nodes.summary: The JC-corrected empirical distance `jcDistance (pHat seq n x y)`.
nodes.title: Jukes–Cantor corrected empirical distance

nodes.summary: The JC transition matrix along a path is the transition matrix of the total length.
nodes.title: Chapman–Kolmogorov along a path

nodes.summary: The JC transition matrix along a path whose branch lengths are listed in `ts`: the product of the branch transition matrices `jcProb μ t`.
nodes.title: Jukes–Cantor transition matrix along a path

nodes.summary: Swapping the two subtrees of the root does not change the likelihood.
nodes.title: Likelihood is invariant under swapping root subtrees

nodes.summary: With the root on the edge between the subtrees `l` and `r`, at distances `s` and `t`, the likelihood is that of the root placed at the root of `l`, with `r` at distance `s + t`.
nodes.title: The root can be pushed to the end of its edge

nodes.summary: Let the root sit on the edge between an internal vertex `x` (at distance `s₁`) and the subtree `C` (at distance `s₂`), where `x` has the subtrees `A` and `B` at distances `a` and `b`. Moving the root to the edge between `x` and `A`, at distance `u₁` from `A` and `u₂` from `x` with `u₁ + u₂ = a`, gives the same likelihood: the unrooted tree and its edge lengths are unchanged (Felsenstein 1981).
nodes.title: Pulley principle, rerooting

nodes.summary: Moving the root along its edge does not change the likelihood (Felsenstein 1981).
nodes.title: Pulley principle, sliding

nodes.summary: Let `d` be the path-length metric of a binary phylogenetic `X`-tree `(G, ι)` with positive edge lengths `w` whose internal edges (no taxon at either end) have length at least `m`. For `μ > 0`, neighbor joining recovers the tree within radius `μ m / 2` of the scaled metric `μ d`. This is `njRun_splits_of_abs_sub_lt` (Atteson 1999) for the edge lengths `μ w`.
nodes.title: Atteson's radius for the scaled tree metric

nodes.summary: Neighbor joining recovers the tree within radius `r` of the dissimilarity `d`: every complete run of neighbor joining on a symmetric dissimilarity `D` with zero diagonal and `|D x y - d x y| < r` for distinct taxa forms exactly the splits of the internal edges of `(G, ι)`. Atteson's theorem gives this for the path-length metric of a binary phylogenetic tree with `r` half the shortest internal edge length…
nodes.title: Neighbor joining recovers a tree within a radius

nodes.summary: The empirical p-distance of the taxa `x, y` over the first `n` sites of the alignment `seq` (`seq i x` is the base of taxon `x` at site `i`): the proportion of sites where they differ.
nodes.title: Empirical p-distance

nodes.summary: For a Markov chain `X → Y → Z` with `X` distributed as `p` (positive), transition matrices `A` (nonnegative) and `B` with unit row sums and nonzero determinants, `d(X, Z) = d(X, Y) + d(Y, Z)`, where `F_XZ = Π_X A B`, `F_XY = Π_X A` and `F_YZ = Π_Y B` with `Y` distributed as `p A`.
nodes.title: Additivity of the LogDet distance along a chain, one step

nodes.summary: The distance of a vertex to itself is `0`: the joint distribution of `X` with itself is the diagonal matrix of its (positive) marginal.
nodes.title: LogDet distance of a vertex to itself is zero

nodes.summary: Additivity of the LogDet distance along a path (Steel 1994; Lockhart et al. 1994): for a Markov chain `v₀ → v₁ → ⋯ → v_n` along a path, with positive initial distribution `p` and nonnegative nonsingular transition matrices `M i` with unit row sums, the LogDet distance between the ends is the sum of the distances of consecutive vertices. The joint distribution of `v₀, v_n` is `Π_{v₀} M 0 ⋯ M (n - 1)`, and that of…
nodes.title: Additivity of the LogDet distance along a path

nodes.summary: Additivity of the LogDet distance at a separating vertex (Steel 1994; Lockhart et al. 1994; Lake 1994). Let `Y` have distribution `p` (positive) and let `X` and `Z` be conditionally independent given `Y`, with transition matrices `M` (from `Y` to `X`) and `N` (from `Y` to `Z`) whose rows sum to `1` and whose determinants are nonzero. The joint distribution matrices are `F_XY = Mᵀ Π_Y`, `F_YZ = Π_Y N` and…
nodes.title: Additivity of the LogDet distance at a separating vertex

nodes.summary: The LogDet (paralinear) distance of a joint distribution matrix `F` (`F i j = ℙ(X = i, Y = j)`): `-log |det F| + (log det Π_X + log det Π_Y) / 2`, where the diagonal marginal matrices have determinants `∏ i, ∑ j, F i j` and `∏ j, ∑ i, F i j`. It is a distance only when `det F ≠ 0` and the marginals are positive; otherwise the value is Lean's totalized logarithm (`log 0 = 0`).
nodes.title: LogDet (paralinear) distance

nodes.summary: On four taxa, the parsimony scores of two quartets differ only on informative patterns: the score on `AB | CD` minus the score on `AC | BD` is `1` on patterns supporting `AC | BD`, `-1` on patterns supporting `AB | CD`, and `0` otherwise; likewise for `AD | BC`.
nodes.title: Difference of parsimony scores of two quartets

nodes.summary: The Fitch parsimony score of the site pattern `σ` on the quartet `((a, b), (c, d))`; it is the small-parsimony score by `Parsimony.fitch_score_eq`.
nodes.title: Fitch parsimony score on a quartet

nodes.summary: The product `M 0 * M 1 * ⋯ * M (n - 1)` of the transition matrices along the first `n` edges of a path.
nodes.title: Product of transition matrices along a path

nodes.summary: The pattern probabilities are nonnegative for change probabilities in `[0, 1]`.
nodes.title: Nonnegativity of site pattern probabilities

nodes.summary: The probability of the site pattern `σ` on the quartet, with the uniform root distribution (the stationary distribution of the symmetric model).
nodes.title: Probability of a site pattern on a quartet

nodes.summary: Swapping the two subtrees of a node does not change its partial likelihoods; with `likelihood_node_comm` this lets the rerooting move `likelihood_reroot` reach either child.
nodes.title: Partial likelihoods are invariant under swapping subtrees

nodes.summary: The rooted quartet `((a, b), (c, d))` with unit costs, for Fitch's algorithm.
nodes.title: Rooted quartet with unit costs

nodes.summary: The quartet `((A, B), (C, D))` on the taxa `0 = A`, `1 = B`, `2 = C`, `3 = D`, with change probabilities `pA, pB, pC, pD` on the pendant edges and `pI` on the internal edge. The root sits at the `AB` end of the internal edge (the edge to the `AB` cherry vertex has change probability `0`); by the pulley principle its position does not matter.
nodes.title: Four-taxon quartet tree model

nodes.summary: The leaf weights of a site pattern `σ`: the indicator of the observed state.
nodes.title: Leaf weights of a site pattern

nodes.summary: The true split `AB | CD` against the third split `AD | BC`: the difference of expected frequencies is `Q (1 - 2 Q) (1 - 2 P)`.
nodes.title: True split against third split frequency difference

nodes.summary: The wrong split `AC | BD` against the third split `AD | BC`: the difference of expected frequencies is `(1 - 2 Q) (P - Q) ^ 2`.
nodes.title: Wrong split against third split frequency difference

nodes.summary: With change probability `P` on the long non-sister branches to `A` and `C` and `Q` on the other three branches, the expected frequency of patterns supporting the wrong split `AC | BD` exceeds that of the true split `AB | CD` by `(1 - 2 Q) (P ^ 2 - Q (1 - Q))`, for all real `P, Q`. This is Felsenstein's equations (16)–(17) (his four-species model has equal probabilities of change `0 → 1` and reversion `1 → 0`).
nodes.title: Felsenstein (1978), the exact comparison

nodes.summary: The expected frequency of the patterns supporting the split `{a, b} | {c, d}`.
nodes.title: Expected frequency of patterns supporting a split

nodes.summary: The pattern probabilities sum to `1`, for all parameters.
nodes.title: Site pattern probabilities sum to one

nodes.summary: The site pattern `σ` supports the split `{a, b} | {c, d}`: `a, b` agree, `c, d` agree, and the two pairs differ (a parsimony-informative pattern for that split).
nodes.title: Site pattern supporting a split

nodes.summary: The symmetric two-state model on one branch: the state changes with probability `p`. As a model, `0 ≤ p ≤ 1/2`.
nodes.title: Symmetric two-state model on a branch

nodes.summary: Under a nonnegative, nonsingular transition matrix, a positive distribution stays positive: every column of `M` has a positive entry. This puts the LogDet logarithms in their domain.
nodes.title: Nonsingular transition matrices preserve positive distributions
